key_insight: Optimizing the noise unraveling can lower the average trajectory magic in noisy random circuits, but a broad tail of high-magic trajectories still remains.
engineering_relevance: For stabilizer-based simulation, the worst-case/high-magic trajectories—not the mean—set the practical computational cost, so unraveling choice matters for algorithm design.
method: Analyzed Haar-random and T-doped random Clifford brickwork circuits under local dephasing noise.
Compared the canonical Pauli-jump unraveling against the full family of minimal Kraus unravelings.
Identified an optimal two-outcome weak-measurement unraveling that minimizes trajectory-averaged stabilizer Rényi entropy.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the optimal unraveling reduces extensive magic density by a p-dependent factor while preserving linear scaling with system size, but leaves a sizable fraction of trajectories near Haar-random magic.
watch_item: Magic is highly broad-distributed across trajectories, so optimizing the mean does not guarantee a large reduction in classical simulation cost.
paper_title: Magic in quantum trajectory unravelings of noisy random quantum circuits
